own_solution.law: Atwood machine with massive pulley: a = (m2 - m1) g / (m1 + m2 + M/2)
assumptions: string does not slip on the pulley (assumed; not stated in the problem)
uniform solid disc pulley, I = M R^2/2

TCD07.regime: max string tension (38.1 N) below the stated limit

T1887.regime: max string tension (38.1 N) below the stated breaking threshold

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The authors' certified answers rely on the assumption that the string does not slip on the pulley, which appears in their assumption list but not in the problem text; without it a frictionlessly sliding string gives a = 2.45 m/s^2 instead of 2.18 m/s^2.

counterexamples: String sliding over a frictionless pulley rim: a = (5-3)(9.8)/8 = 2.45 m/s^2, pulley mass and radius both irrelevant.
notes: All certified answers check under the no-slip model: base 19.6/9 = 2.17778; R with q = 0.4, 0.8, 1.2 kg added to m1: 15.68/9.4 = 1.66809, 11.76/9.8 = 1.2, 7.84/10.2 = 0.768627. Radius cancels (I/r^2 = M/2) for 8, 12, 16 cm. K regime: max tension is 38.1 N (right side), below 120, 200 and 300 N, so all listed values lie inside the regime. Minimal pairs T572A/TBE0C and T9AFE/T707F state the same 0.8 kg and differ only in attachment. The only defect is that the no-slip condition, listed by the authors as an assumption, is not stated in the problem; under admission rule 1 this decides the answer (2.18 vs 2.45 m/s^2), so I keep my pass-1 verdict. If the panel treats no-slip as implied by giving the pulley's mass, the item would otherwise be CERTIFIED_AND_VALIDATED. No disagreement with pass 1.
